title: Meta-UCF: Unified Task-Conditioned LoRA Generation for Continual Learning in Large Language Models
claim: A single hypernetwork turns a task embedding into adapter weights, and losses on query data update only that generator.
layout: Single panel, flows left-to-right then loops back; color-coded arrows with legend
description: A single-panel system diagram with a legend strip at the bottom. At top left, stacks of books mark previous tasks. These are sampled into a support set (blue database icon), which passes through a grey frozen backbone to give a task embedding e_k. The embedding feeds an orange Meta-Conditioned Parameter Generator box with a flame icon for trainable. The generator infers the LoRA matrices (A_l, B_l), which update the green LoRA block. That block sits beside the blue Pretrained Backbone in a dashed box, and the two outputs are summed into a Prediction. An incoming task's query set (yellow-blue database) feeds the backbone. Red arrows carry the Prediction and LoRA outputs into a pink Overall Loss box containing L_orh, L_task, L_ctr and R_k. A green backprop arrow returns to the generator. The legend distinguishes feedforward, loss calculation, learning process, trainable and frozen. Colored boxes and snowflake and flame icons draw the eye first.
caption: Meta-UCF pipeline: a support set from memory yields the task embedding ek, the generator gΦ produces LoRA updates (Al, Bl) for the frozen backbone, and the current task’s query batch drives losses {Ltask, Lorth, Lctr, Rk} whose gradient updates only the generator.
abstract: Large language models are increasingly deployed in settings where newtasks arrive continuously, yet existing parameter-efficient finetuning (PEFT) methods either bloat linearly with the task horizon or sacrifice deep adaptation, leaving catastrophic forgetting unresolved. We aim to achieve memory-constant, on-the-fly adaptation for a frozen LLM facing an unbounded stream of tasks. To this end we propose Meta-Unified Contrastive Finetuning(Meta-UCF), which encodes each task into a lightweight layer-normalised mean embedding and feeds it to a single hypernetwork that instantly generates rank-r LoRA updates for every transformer layer; a meta-contrastive coupled with orthogonality objective further steers task embeddings into near-orthogonal directions, preserving past knowledge without inner-loop gradients. On four benchmark streams—Std-CL 5, Seq-GLUE 7, Long-CL 15 and TRACE-8—Meta-UCF raises average accuracy by up to 2.2 pp and cuts forgetting by 13% relative to the strongest LoRA baseline, while using the parameters of a single adapter. By decoupling continual learning from parameter growth, Meta-UCF provides a practical path toward scalable, low-resource lifelong language modelling.
